clips.caption: Jordan Hill introduces the concept of agentic observability, emphasizing the need for visualizing AI agent workflows in real systems.
He explains how ephemeral Cloudflare Workers enable task execution and data reporting, forming the backbone of his observability system.
Jordan highlights the importance of simplifying complex AI concepts for non-technical stakeholders to ensure adoption and understanding.
He details the architecture using Cloudflare Queue, D1, and KV for event capture, long-term storage, and fast access to leaderboard data.
Jordan draws parallels to horsepower in cars, advocating for measurable benchmarks to compare and improve agentic systems.
He presents a live leaderboard and 3D diagram of his Cloudflare setup, showing real-time performance and system flow.
Jordan explains how run IDs enable traceability across agents and discusses the trade-offs between real-time updates and practicality.
He breaks down Cloudflare’s components—queue, D1, KV, R2, durable objects—and how they work together without complex orchestration.
Jordan demonstrates an interactive, animated diagram of his system, allowing users to explore components and their relationships.
He shares examples like automated media buying and event attendance tracking, concluding with a vision for standardized, visual AI workflows.
